title: SWE-1.5: THE SPEED ERA
lede: October 29, 2025. A frontier-size model — hundreds of billions of parameters — served at up to 950 tokens per second on Cerebras wafer-scale silicon. SWE-1.5's claim was not that it was the smartest model in the room; it was that the smartest model in the room had always been allowed to be slow, and that stopped here.
body:
h2. THE SPEED CLAIM

table(statrow).
|950 tok/s|6×|13×|
|peak serve rate|faster than haiku 4.5|faster than sonnet 4.5|

p. The stack was co-designed end-to-end — %(cyan)model, inference, and agent harness% treated as one system. Serving came via a partnership with %(amber)Cerebras%, whose wafer-scale hardware runs the model at rates conventional GPU clusters don't reach. The pitch to users was simple: you no longer choose between an AI that thinks fast and one that thinks well.

h2. THE FALCON ALPHA AFFAIR

p. Before launch, the model beta-tested undercover. Windsurf users noticed a mysterious entry in the model picker labeled %(hl)Falcon Alpha% — an unannounced checkpoint collecting real-world telemetry. The annals record this as the moment the lab learned to dress its research in a trench coat.

h2. THE SUPPORTING CAST

p. SWE-1.5 didn't arrive alone. Two weeks earlier — %(ok)October 16, 2025% — Cognition released %(cyan)SWE-grep%, an agentic model trained purely for rapid context engineering: the retrieval specialist that finds the right code before the flagship reasons about it. The pattern of pairing a big thinker with a fast fetcher persists in the product to this day — see the "invisible models":products.html exhibit.

bq. Developers shouldn't have to choose between an AI that thinks fast and one that thinks well. %(dim)— Cognition, October 29, 2025%

h2. THE ARCHIVE NOTES

* Availability: Windsurf model picker, all tiers.
* Architecture: undisclosed; 'frontier-size, hundreds of billions of parameters' is the on-record figure.
* Legacy: the speed bar it set (950 tok/s) became the default expectation — every later SWE release is measured against it.

p. Next hall: same silicon, smoother manners — "SWE-1.6":swe-16.html.
